A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, with POCO renamed BOPO in v3. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original JSP, TSP, and FJSP experiments, component ablations, and training curves. Its appendices include model-efficiency, runtime, and hybrid-rollout results.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds INViT-based TSP evaluations in Figure 2 and controlled TSP experiments in Appendix F.

M1.justification: Hybrid rollout, uniform filtering, best-anchored pairing, Algorithm 1, the objective-scaled loss, and the MGL architecture remain unchanged. BOPO is a renaming; applying the training paradigm to INViT adds an experimental configuration without a documented modification of the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: The existing scheduling benchmarks, uniform TSP instances, and TSPLIB evaluation remain. v3 substantially extends distributional coverage with generated cluster, explosion, and implosion TSP instances, alongside uniform instances, evaluated at 1,000, 5,000, and 10,000 nodes in Figure 2.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds Concorde and DABL, including augmented DABL results. Figure 2 introduces comparisons against original and retrained RL-based INViT-2V, while Appendix F adds POMO+ using hybrid rollout and uniform filtering. These expand the evaluated comparator set beyond citations already present in v1.

E3.justification: Existing experiments retain their stated settings. New evaluations introduce INViT-2V with D=1, B=64, K=8 and doubled epochs, a retrained RL control with matching batch size, and larger TSP scales. Appendix F adds reduced-rollout settings B=20/50 and a control applying standard POMO loss to filtered solutions.

E4.justification: Figure 2 adds distribution-shift and scale-generalization analyses on another backbone. Appendix F tests whether fewer rollouts suffice and whether rollout/filtering alone explains the advantage over RL. These materially extend the existing component, loss, hyperparameter, and hybrid-rollout analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or an uncertainty-estimation procedure. The added results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Matched existing benchmark scores are retained, but substantial new results appear. Figure 2 reports a 5.13% gap for BOPO-trained INViT on uniform TSP with 1,000 nodes versus 6.31% for retrained RL. Table 13 reports TSP50 gaps of 0.081% for POMO+ and 0.009% for both BOPO configurations. Table 2 adds Concorde and DABL results.

T1.justification: Appendix A corrects successor-operation indexing in the formal JSP and FJSP directed-edge definitions. Appendix C also corrects the textual association of d and s with DPO and SimPO. The substantive loss and gradient derivations remain; the added REINFORCE formula mainly restates existing background.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims of improved sample efficiency, architecture-independent preference training, and strong performance on JSP, TSP, and FJSP. The new name foregrounds components already present in v1 rather than introducing a different central contribution.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations distinguishing pairwise learning from filtered RL, cautions that its filtering may not transfer to general RL methods, and argues that small problems need fewer rollouts. It also suggests margin-related overfitting as an explanation for SimPO's DMU performance. The existing rollout-cost limitation remains.

D1.justification: v1 only promises future code release; v3 supplies a repository link and reports that the PyTorch implementation and trained models for each problem are available. This substantially expands documented resource access. v3 also specifies the added INViT training configuration; existing hardware and scheduling-model details remain.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds concurrent work by Pan et al. (2025), distinguishing BOPO through its pairing strategy and objective-guided loss, and adds Chen et al. (2025a,b). The broader related-work organization and positioning remain largely intact.

P1.justification: The title and terminology change from POCO to BOPO, with corresponding edits throughout the abstract, headings, and prose. Local explanations, acknowledgements, and Appendix F are added, while the main section sequence and most existing exposition remain.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is relabeled and relocated; the original training-curve Figures 2 and 3 become panels of v3 Figure 3. v3 adds a four-panel Figure 2 and Table 13 and expands Table 2. Other displays are largely retained or relocated within the same overall layout.

improvement.justification: The INViT evaluations and Appendix F controls strengthen an already substantial empirical study, while documented code and model access improves reproducibility information. Some comparative prose remains too broad: DABL beats unaugmented BOPO throughout Table 2, and original INViT beats BOPO on the 5,000-node implosion case in Figure 2. The added evidence provides a clear but limited net improvement.
